 Vermont trains 70 benefit assisters amid changes to federal programs 
 By WCAX News Team Published : Nov. 17, 2026 at 2:54 PM EST | Updated : 2 hours ago Share Add Us On Google Add as a preferred source on Google BURLINGTON, Vt. (WCAX) - State money is supporting a program that helps eligible Vermonters access benefits.
 President Trump’s Big Beautiful Bill passed last year included cuts to 3SquaresVT and Medicaid, among other low-income programs
 An estimated 2,500 Vermonters lost SNAP benefits, and 45,000 could lose Medicaid coverage, in addition to the hundreds of immigrant households already impacted.
 That’s where benefit assisters come in, helping connect people with benefits.
 “It is not easy to navigate 3SquaresVT or Medicaid. The applications are complex and require a lot of information, and the paperwork people have to submit to keep their benefits has only increased because of H.R. 1. Benefit assisters are experts in navigating these systems and requirements,” said Anore Horton with Hunger Free Vermont.
 When the president’s spending bill passed, the Vermont Legislature invested in the state’s benefit assisters program. Since September, 70 new benefit assisters have been trained and certified.
